punchline: Zhuge Liang turned back an army with open gates and a lute, because his reputation was doing the fighting.
thirty_sec: Everyone quotes Law 5 of Robert Greene's The 48 Laws of Power as 'guard your reputation.' The full law goes further. It says to open holes in your rivals' reputations, then stand aside and let public opinion finish them. P.T. Barnum did something like this by planting doubts through the press. The telling part is 'stand aside.' Even Greene's method only works if nobody sees who started it, because an attacker who gets noticed pays a price.
question: Why would a book about ruthless power still tell you to hide your hand when you damage someone's name?
